subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 7-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department 5 minutes after eating a peanut butter cookie at school. He has lip and tongue swelling, diffuse urticaria, and audible wheezing, and his blood pressure is 78/40 mm Hg. He has a history of atopic dermatitis and allergic rhinitis, and a serum tryptase level drawn later is elevated. The reaction resolves after intramuscular epinephrine.
question: The rapid onset of this patient's symptoms is initiated by cross-linking of which of the following structures on the surface of his mast cells and basophils?

options.text: Secretory component bound to dimeric IgA
Fc gamma receptors bound to IgG immune complexes
Pentameric IgM bound to complement fragments
Surface IgD acting as a B-cell antigen receptor

explanation_correct: In type I hypersensitivity, peanut allergens cross-link IgE already bound to high-affinity Fc epsilon RI receptors on mast cells and basophils. This triggers degranulation and release of preformed mediators such as histamine and tryptase, producing urticaria, bronchospasm, and hypotension; IgE switching depends on Th2 cytokines including IL-4 and IL-13.

explanation_incorrect.A: Secretory component plus dimeric IgA forms secretory IgA, which neutralizes pathogens at mucosal surfaces and does not arm mast cells for immediate degranulation.
explanation_incorrect.C: Fc gamma receptors bind IgG and participate in opsonization and type II and III hypersensitivity, not in the IgE-dependent immediate reaction seen here.
explanation_incorrect.D: IgM is a complement-fixing pentamer involved in early humoral responses and immune-complex disease; it is not the mast-cell-bound isotype that triggers anaphylaxis.
explanation_incorrect.E: IgD is expressed on naive B cells and serves as an antigen receptor; it is not present on mast cells and does not mediate their degranulation.

educationalObjective: Immediate type I hypersensitivity is initiated when an allergen cross-links IgE bound to Fc epsilon RI on mast cells and basophils.
